# Generate blocked spatial index

Generate blocked spatial index

## Usage

``` r
generate_block_sp_index(covars, cv_fold = NULL, blocks = NULL, block_id = NULL)
```

## Arguments

- covars:

  data.frame-like object with `lon`, `lat`, and `time` columns.

- cv_fold:

  integer(1). Number of folds for cross-validation.

- blocks:

  numeric(2)/sf/SpatVector configuration of blocks.

- block_id:

  character(1). The unique identifier of each block.

## Value

data.frame-like object (same class as `covars`) with a `sp_index` column

## Details

"Block" in this function refers to a group of contiguous
spatial/temporal entities. Regardless of `mode` value (should be one of
`"spatial"` or `"spatiotemporal"`), the index column will be named
"sp_index". `block_id` should be set with a proper field name when
blocks is a sf or SpatVector object. When `cv_fold` is an integer, then
the *unique* `lon`/`lat` coordinates in `covars` are clustered (not
every row), so the result is unaffected by how many times each location
was observed — this keeps the block assignment correct for
irregular/unbalanced spacetime panels. Location matching when
broadcasting the cluster/block id back onto `covars` is by exact
`lon`/`lat` equality; coordinates that jitter slightly across repeated
observations of "the same" site should be rounded/snapped beforehand.
When `cv_fold` is an integer, the result object will include attributes
(accessible with `attr` function) about "dbscan_eps" and
"dbscan_minPts".

## Author

Insang Song

## Examples

``` r
data(spdat)
covars <- spdat
covars_block <- generate_block_sp_index(covars, cv_fold = 5)
covars_block
```
